question: Sacubitril/valsartan (an ARNI) should NOT be used concurrently with an ACE inhibitor because combining them causes dangerous accumulation of bradykinin, risking life-threatening angioedema.

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: This statement is true. The combination of sacubitril (neprilysin inhibitor) + ACE inhibitor blocks bradykinin degradation at two enzymatic steps simultaneously, dramatically increasing angioedema risk. Guidelines require a 36-hour ACEi-free window before initiating ARNI.
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: Correct. Sacubitril inhibits neprilysin (which normally degrades bradykinin and natriuretic peptides), while valsartan blocks AT1 receptors. If an ACEi is added, bradykinin cannot be degraded by either ACE (blocked by ACEi) or neprilysin (blocked by sacubitril), leading to catastrophic bradykinin accumulation and angioedema. A 36-hour washout from ACEi before starting ARNI is mandatory.
